rows.label: Derivation
rows.text: **Brassicaceae (Cruciferae).** Mustard family: flowers with four petals in a cross, six stamens (four long, two short), and silique fruits; mustard oil gives the pungent taste.  ·  **Fabaceae (Papilionoideae).** Pea family: papilionaceous corolla (standard, wings, keel), ten stamens (nine fused), legume fruits, and root nodules housing nitrogen-fixing Rhizobium.

rows.label: Study notes
rows.text: **Solanaceae.** Potato family: five epipetalous stamens with swollen anthers, bicarpellary superior ovary, and berry or capsule fruits; tomato, brinjal and chilli belong here.  ·  **Liliaceae.** Lily family: monocots with parallel-veined leaves, trimerous flowers with six tepals, and superior trilocular ovary; onion, garlic and tulip are examples.  ·  **Economic importance.** These four families supply food crops, spices, medicines (alkaloids), oils and ornamentals — they are among the most useful angiosperm families.
